title: A trap a competent agent recovers from unaided pays nothing in a ledger
claim: Recording a trap changes an agent's answer only when the trap is both absent from the model's training and not recoverable from evidence available on the machine within the agent's budget; traps failing either condition are retrieved correctly, cited correctly, and change nothing.
appliesTo: A retrieval corpus of engineering traps consulted by a capable coding agent that can run commands on the affected machine.
expectation: A corpus that retrieves the right trap, ranked first, in response to an agent's own unprompted query, improves what the agent does. Accuracy of retrieval is the thing to optimise.
reality: Retrieval was not the binding constraint. Across three traps and twenty-two trials the agent asked for the ledger unprompted, got the correct finding ranked first, and cited it by id in the code it wrote -- and the arm without the ledger was equally correct every time. Retrieval accuracy was near perfect and the outcome delta was zero, because in all three cases a capable agent could reach the same answer without help.
mechanism: There are two independent routes around a recorded trap and a finding only pays when both are shut. The first is training: a trap documented in a widely-read manual is already in the weights. The second is local recovery: a trap whose evidence sits on the machine can be derived by an agent willing to spend turns on it -- a parse error printed on stderr, or a TLS certificate whose issuer names the intercepting gateway. The second route is the one that is easy to forget, because it makes an environment-specific trap -- exactly the kind a ledger exists for -- still recoverable, just expensively.
workaround: Judge a candidate finding on both routes before admitting it, not on how surprising it felt: is it absent from public documentation, AND could an agent on the affected machine derive it from available evidence within a plausible budget? If the answer to the second is yes, the finding may still be worth keeping, but its payoff is a cost saving and must be measured as one -- turns, wall clock, tokens -- because measuring it as correctness will show nothing. Note that a two-arm correctness comparison is the wrong instrument for that, and needs far more trials than a correctness comparison would.

evidence.output:
reachability — control 3/3   with cairn 4/4
REFUSED (not counted) — control 2, cairn 1
evidence.note: cairn-0001, an allowlist proxy whose CONNECT 403 arrives as a transport error. Environment-specific and absent from any training set, so the first route was shut -- and both arms still answered correctly, because the control arm derived it locally: it ran positive controls against allowlisted hosts and read the TLS certificate, whose issuer names the egress gateway.

cairn-0005. Silent by construction -- the build passes and the page renders -- but force-dynamic is in the Next.js documentation, so the first route was open. The cairn arm asked unprompted, got cairn-0005 first, and cited it in a comment; the control arm wrote the same route config from memory.
cairn-0003. Loud: a regex parse error and exit 2. The model reached for grep -F; told the project mandates ripgrep, it reached for rg -F. Locally recoverable in one turn.

check.command: Run a two-arm trial on a recorded trap: identical task and model, one arm with corpus retrieval and one without, several trials per arm, scoring the deliverable rather than whether the tool was called.
check.confirmedIf: the arm without retrieval reaches the correct outcome as often as the arm with it, on a trap that is publicly documented or derivable from evidence on the machine
check.refutedIf: the arm without retrieval is measurably wrong more often on such a trap

observations.note: Twenty-two trials over three traps chosen to remove one suspected confound at a time -- first loudness, then public documentation. Every arm with retrieval queried the ledger unprompted and got the intended finding ranked first; no arm without it was ever wrong. The one axis showing any daylight was steps to the answer, and it is not significant here: control took 13, 14 and 15 tool calls, the ledger arm 9, 12, 12 and 14, with overlapping ranges at n=3 and n=4. Recorded as suggestive and nothing more. Scope is environment-specific because this is one model against one small corpus; a weaker model, or a trap satisfying both conditions, could behave differently and has not been tested.

environment.note: claude-opus-5 via the Messages API, bash tool plus optional cairn_search over a 33-finding corpus.

triggers: scoring the deliverable rather than whether the tool was called
